newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia corn prices set to weaken in face of glut.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia corn prices set to weaken in face of glut.

text.p: Corn prices look set to fall in Malaysia until the end of July as few signs of take-up demand have emerged in a market overstocked with the grain, traders said on Tuesday.
Stockpile of maize in warehouses throughout Malaysia were close to 200,000 tonnes on Tuesday, and new arrivals were aggravating the situation, the traders said.

The price of bulk corn, ex-factories/godowns in Malaysia's central region, was trading at a lower end of 375 ringgit ($149.11) to a higher 385 ringgit per tonne C & F, compared to 380/385 ringgit a week earlier.
"It's breaking...from next week I think we'll see a steady fall of five to ten ringgit every week until end of July," said a trader.
Last week, one trader said it could take up to mid-July or even early August to clear the existing stocks as well as new arrivals projected over the next four weeks.

"For the moment, we have about 30,000 to 50,000 tonnes (of maize) arriving a week," said the trader. "Once we have a clear idea on when the intake stops, then we'll know when prices could firm again."
Soymeal was trading quietly again this week but the price of the imported material was down to 860 ringgit from 870 the week before. Local soymeal was maintained at 880 ringgit.
"A" grade wheat in bags was unchanged at 730 ringgit. "B" grade wheat was also steady at 430 ringgit.
